name: Pexiganan (MSI-78)
haemolysis_value: Human erythrocytes: 10-20% at 13 µg/ml; 50-60% at 50 µg/ml
known_stability_notes: Salt/serum exposure and proteolysis can reduce in vivo exposure.
known_solubility_notes: Generally soluble at screening concentrations in aqueous buffer.
notes: Positive benchmark with broad antibacterial activity. Clinical phase III efficacy did not exceed standard care.

name: Magainin 2 (magainin-II)
known_stability_notes: Short cationic helix; known to be protease-sensitive but manageable with straightforward formulation.
notes: Positive linear benchmark with clear antibacterial activity and low haemolytic signal.

name: LL-37 (human cathelicidin)
known_stability_notes: Human derived sequence; activity can diminish in physiologic salts and serum.
known_solubility_notes: Soluble in water but binds host proteins/lipids, reducing free concentration.
notes: Positive natural reference scaffold with broad antibacterial activity and manageable baseline properties.

name: Iseganan (IB-367)
haemolysis_value: Human erythrocytes: 90-100% at 99.6 µM; 0-10% at 2 µM
known_stability_notes: Disulfide-rich scaffold raises synthetic complexity and oxidative heterogeneity.
known_solubility_notes: Formulation sensitive at higher concentrations; free peptide tends to be limited by cytotoxicity window.
notes: Liability-oriented scaffold: activity present but narrow therapeutic window and high host-cell risk.

name: Temporin-SHf
known_stability_notes: Very short peptide; lower proteolytic stability and rapid loss in complex matrices.
known_solubility_notes: High hydrophobic content makes formulation and selectivity control challenging.
notes: Near-negative/weak example: poor antifungal potency (MIC >100 µM) and likely weak translational potential.
